explanation.summary: A sudden ~2× increase in traffic for ID 0x6E0 together with a sharp drop in payload entropy and faster inter‑arrival times suggests an attacker injecting fabricated frames on this ID.

claims.text: The detector highlighted strong rate inflation (0.583) and reduced payload entropy (0.49) for the window.
ID 0x6E0 transmitted at 202 msg/s versus a baseline of ~100 msg/s, a 2.02× increase.
The payload entropy for 0x6E0 fell from 6.952 to 3.746, indicating far less variability in the injected data.
Mean inter‑arrival time for 0x6E0 halved (4.975 ms vs 10 ms baseline), showing a faster transmission rate.
No new unknown CAN IDs appear; other IDs show only sparse activity and do not drive the alert.
Sampled frames for 0x6E0 contain low‑entropy payload patterns (e.g., repeated 0xFF bytes, repetitive 0x03 values).
The combination of elevated rate, reduced entropy, and unchanged ID set matches the signature of a spoofing (fabrication) attack.

explanation.recommended_action: Log the event and isolate the source node transmitting ID 0x6E0. Deploy a CAN‑IDS rule to filter or rate‑limit this ID, and perform a physical inspection of the bus for unauthorized transceivers. Correlate with vehicle logs to determine any functional impact.
